- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or fails to anticipate sharp drops; increase early forecast sensitivity to recent lows.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 2.08–2.10) with exaggerated 30d overshoots; cap forecast peaks at 1.5x recent high or 2.0x recent mean.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon; if forecast is >1.5x recent 18d average, apply downward correction by 20–40% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Sentiment volatility (alternating 0.67/0.33) correlates with model oscillation; smooth forecasts by averaging 3–5 prior days’ values when sentiment is unstable.
- If sentiment is uniformly positive for 3+ days, model tends to overpredict; apply a 10–20% downward bias to 30d forecast unless price is near historical high.
- If sentiment is uniformly negative for 3+ days, model underpredicts; apply 10–20% upward bias to 30d forecast unless price is near historical low.
